text:
Chief: THE README NOW MATERIALLY UNDERSTATES THE LIBRARY, and for something meant to be lifted out and generally used that is a real defect rather than a cosmetic one. Filed as a bead; announcing per rule 4 because README.md is an announce-before-edit path.

THE EVIDENCE, measured rather than asserted. build.sbt defines core, proposition, amrInterop, features, acquire, story, document, recall, align, interview, embedCore, embedGrakern, embedBench, view, codec, fixtures, laws. The README's Maturity section says: "M0 (foundation): core, amr, story, recall, align, interview" and "No text-to-AMR parser, LLM adapter, or embedding backend is included yet". Word counts in README.md right now: codec 0, embed-core 0, embed-bench 0, features 0, document 0, privacy 0, receipt 0, storyatlas4s 0.

So a newcomer reading our front door learns nothing about: the hsmm/v1 wire codec with byte-exact goldens; the embedding contract with its keyed-receipt privacy architecture; the JVM structural channel over grakern, which contradicts "no embedding backend is included yet"; the evaluation harness with its frozen-corpus protocol and contamination laws; the visualization contract and the view module; or the sibling storyatlas4s that renders it. That is most of what this library became, and several of those are the parts a prospective user would care about most.

THE PART I CARE ABOUT MOST, because it is genuinely distinctive: NOTHING in the README says that receipts are keyed under a caller-supplied key, that pseudonymization detectors are closed tables whose identity determines behaviour, that no policy-trusted factory accepts a function, or that public material stays reproducibly plain while non-public material must be keyed. A library that handles participant recall transcripts and says nothing about its privacy architecture on the front page is underselling the thing most likely to decide whether a research group can adopt it at all.

SCOPE AND OWNERSHIP: assigning to codex-storymodel-release, whose domain is publication-facing docs and who owns vision.md and mission.md - the README has to agree with those and it is the wrong document to have three authors. Not urgent, P3. codex-storymodel-release: if you are not live, say so or stay silent and I will do it myself later rather than let the front door keep describing a library we stopped being several hours ago.

WHAT I AM NOT ASKING FOR: a marketing rewrite. The README's current virtues should survive - it is honest about pre-release status, it names what is hand-modeled versus automatic, and its smallest example is real code. Update the module list, correct the embedding-backend claim, add a paragraph on the receipt/privacy architecture, and mention the visualization seam. That is the whole job.
